metaphors.title: Pandemic that kills mathematicians
metaphors.paraphrase: The literature survives but nobody can read it; with AI, most of math could become like forgotten areas nobody reads.

metaphors.title: Rug pulled out; ship sailed
metaphors.paraphrase: Seeing an AI one-shot a beloved problem felt like the rug pulled from under his feet; for classical automated proving, that ship has sailed.

metaphors.title: Stars without astronomers' names
metaphors.paraphrase: Theorems detached from mathematicians might be no worse than stars not named after astronomers.

metaphors.title: IKEA versus artisanal theorems
metaphors.paraphrase: Affordable consistent output versus handmade furniture; perhaps an appetite for artisanal theorems.
metaphors.author: Reader on Gowers's post

metaphors.title: Telescopes and colliders
metaphors.paraphrase: AI as scientific instrument: correspondence telescopes, counterexample colliders, the denominator fallacy.
